cf.title: [Patch] Fix pg_get_multixact_stats() over-reporting members on a hot standby

input.subject: [Patch] Fix pg_get_multixact_stats() over-reporting members on a hot standby

verdict_reasoning: No objection survived at levels 1a, 1b or 2. The problem is stated and reproduced in message #1, and the thread agreed in messages #2 and #3 to raise an error during recovery, which copies the existing xlogfuncs.c practice. The function is new in 19, so no released behaviour changes. Confidence is medium because v2, which carries the agreed design, is not attached.

brief.title: Fix pg_get_multixact_stats() over-reporting members on a hot standby
brief.problem: On a hot standby, MultiXactState->oldestOffset is not maintained and stays at 0, so pg_get_multixact_stats() reports num_members as nextOffset. num_members and members_size are too large, while num_mxids and oldest_multixact are correct. This misleads anyone who monitors multixact member space on a standby.
brief.proposed_design: v1 updates oldestOffset while replaying XLOG_MULTIXACT_TRUNCATE_ID, and TrimMultiXact() still recomputes it at end of recovery. The value still reads 0 until the first truncation record arrives and again after a standby restart. The thread then agreed to raise an error when the function runs during recovery, which the author says matches an unposted v2.
user_visible_surface: pg_get_multixact_stats(): num_members and members_size become correct on a standby once a truncation record is replayed (v1).
pg_get_multixact_stats(): raises an ERROR with ERRCODE_OBJECT_NOT_IN_PREREQUISITE_STATE when called during recovery (agreed direction, v2).
Error message and hint reused from xlogfuncs.c, so no new translatable strings.
author_claims: On REL_19_BETA3 the standby showed about 17.5M members and 84 MB while the primary showed zero for the same data.
With v1 the standby and primary return matching results for the same workload.
Promoting the standby fixes the values at once, because oldestOffset is computed at end of recovery.
Multixact numbers are not actionable on a standby, since freezing and vacuum run on the primary, so an error is more honest than wrong numbers.
brief.thread_state: Heikki and Michael replied; Heikki rejected the redo-only fix because the window can be long and returns after restart. Michael said he would make the function error during recovery, and the author says v2 already does this.
unclear: v2 is mentioned but not attached, so its exact behaviour, tests and documentation changes are not visible.
The material does not say whether the docs for pg_get_multixact_stats() will state that it fails on a standby.
Nobody says whether existing monitoring that calls the function on standbys needs to handle the new error.
No regression or TAP test is mentioned for either v1 or the error path.
Storing oldestOffset in the control file was raised and deferred, with no plan for a later release.

touch_points.label: WAL / replication / standby
touch_points.reason: v1 changes replay of XLOG_MULTIXACT_TRUNCATE_ID in multixact.c, and the agreed v2 changes the function's behaviour on a standby.

touch_points.label: backpatchability
touch_points.reason: The entry is a bug fix targeted at 19, where pg_get_multixact_stats() is new and still in beta.

touch_points.label: maintenance burden ("who maintains this in 10 years")
doesn't fit what Postgres is about (extension / external tool / already solved)

questions: Can you post v2, so reviewers can see the exact error behaviour of pg_get_multixact_stats() during recovery?
Does v2 keep v1's update of oldestOffset while replaying XLOG_MULTIXACT_TRUNCATE_ID, or does it drop that change?
Will the documentation of pg_get_multixact_stats() state that the function raises an error during recovery?
Does v2 add a test that calls pg_get_multixact_stats() on a standby and checks the error?
Is the loss of the correct num_mxids and oldest_multixact on a standby acceptable, given that only num_members and members_size are wrong today?

committability.owner_note: Heikki Linnakangas and Michael Paquier replied in the thread, and Michael said he would make the function raise an error during recovery.
committability.liability: Small: one recovery check in a monitoring function that is new in 19, with an error message reused from xlogfuncs.c. The deferred control-file field for oldestOffset stays open for a later release.
committability.author_follow_up: The author says in message #1 that he wants to help but may be slow to respond, and invites others to take the patch over.

priority.reason: The fix corrects wrong output from a function that is new in 19, so it is best settled before release. The patch touches one file, the agreed design adds no new state or strings, and a committer has offered to make the change.

provisional_note: v2 is not attached, so its error check, documentation and tests could not be judged. Whether v1's redo-path update of oldestOffset remains in the final patch, and whether it is safe during replay, also needs the code.
disclosure: Prepared by an AI harness; treat as a devil's advocate, not a verdict.

precedents_retrieved.title: Make VACUUM remove MultiXacts with updater XIDs more eagerly
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch changes FreezeMultiXactId() so that VACUUM removes a MultiXact outright when all of its members are older than OldestXmin, instead of leaving it in place with FRM_NOOP processing. The goal is to get more use out of each GetMultiXactIdMembers() call and to remove more Multis that have updater XIDs, since OldestMxact can be held back much longer than OldestXmin.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The visible messages do not show why. The thread ends when Peter Geoghegan creates the CF entry. No message shows a reviewer objecting to this patch or the author explaining the withdrawal. Andres Freund's objections in the thread concern the separate patch that skips the TransactionIdDidCommit() sanity checks.

precedents_retrieved.summary: Revert XactLockTableWait context setup in conditional multixact wait

precedents_retrieved.title: Enhance statistics reset functions to return reset timestamp
precedents_retrieved.objectors: Michael Paquier, Andres Freund, David Rowley
precedents_retrieved.summary: Make the core statistics reset functions, such as pg_stat_reset(), pg_stat_reset_shared() and pg_stat_reset_replication_slot(), return the reset time as timestamptz, as pg_stat_statements_reset() already does. Functions that take a backend PID or slot name would return NULL for invalid input.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The author withdrew the patches after objections. Michael Paquier said most of these functions never fail, and the reset time is already in the stats views. Andres Freund saw no convincing use case and said granular resets were a mistake to build on. David Rowley agreed, said that resetting stats to track activity is wrong and can affect autovacuum, and suggested logging values and taking differences with LAG().
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
-1 - I think it was a mistake to introduce support for granular resets, we
shouldn't bury ourselves deeper.

precedents_retrieved.title: Simplify standby state machine a bit in WaitForWALToBecomeAvailable()
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch makes the standby state machine in WaitForWALToBecomeAvailable() set currentSource to XLOG_FROM_PG_WAL after a failed archive read, so XLogFileReadAnyTLI() no longer falls back to pg_wal itself. The current source is then passed to XLogFileReadAnyTLI() directly, without the XLOG_FROM_ANY special case.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Michael Paquier showed that the patch undoes commit 4d894b41. On HEAD, XLogFileReadAnyTLI() checks the archive and then pg_wal for each timeline in turn. With the patch it checks the archive for all timelines and only then pg_wal, so a segment with a higher TLI in pg_wal is no longer preferred. The author agreed and withdrew the patch.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: And this patch basically undoes that, meaning that we would basically look at the archives first for all the expected TLIs, but only if no files were found in pg_wal/.

precedents_retrieved.title: SQL function which allows to distinguish a server being in point in time recovery mode and an ordinary replica
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch adds a SQL function that reports whether standby.signal was found at startup, so users can tell a server in point-in-time recovery from a streaming replica, since pg_is_in_recovery() returns true for both. After review, it was reworked to replace the recovery booleans in XLogRecoveryCtlData with a bits32 flag set and to expose those flags as a text[] array.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The thread had two commitfest entries, and vignesh C closed the second one as a duplicate. The visible messages show no objection that ended the work. At the end, open review points included missing test patches and a test failing against v6.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: I have closed the second entry at [2].

precedents_retrieved.title: Implement type input functions for extended statistics types
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch adds input functions for the extended statistics types pg_ndistinct, pg_dependencies and pg_mcv_list, so that dumped extended statistics can be restored. It parses pg_ndistinct and pg_dependencies with a new yacc grammar and reads pg_mcv_list through byteain().
precedents_retrieved.objection: The author withdrew the entry after Tomas Vondra and Tom Lane said dump and reload should start with regular statistics, and that it needs a plan for statistics whose format changes between major versions or whose meaning depends on the environment, such as collation. The patch also had build warnings and failed regression tests, and Andres Freund reported that it crashed in CI. The thread has no author reply after these comments.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
And yes, the main
stumbling block is that you need to have a plan for stats changing
across versions, or even just environmental issues.

precedents_retrieved.title: Fix cancelled queries when hot_standby_feedback = on
precedents_retrieved.summary: With hot_standby_feedback = on, standby queries still get cancelled when vacuum truncates a heap on the primary, because the AccessExclusiveLock taken for truncation is replayed on the standby. The final patch adds a new lock level, ACCESS EXCLUSIVE LOCAL, that vacuum uses for heap truncation and that is not WAL-logged, so standby queries must tolerate concurrent truncation.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Tom Lane showed that letting scans run during truncation leaves a race: concurrent scans can load to-be-truncated pages back into shared buffers before ftruncate, and reading past EOF on a standby can extend the relation. Alexander Korotkov agreed the patch had to be revised and sketched a new truncation design, but Robert Haas called it fragile and doubted it prevents stale buffers from being taken as valid. No new version followed, the existing patch failed initdb, and the entry was closed.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: If we ever have valid-looking buffers in shared_buffers after the corresponding data has been truncated away on disk, we've got to make sure that nobody ever confuses one of them with an actually-valid buffer.

precedents_retrieved.title: SQL function which allows to distinguish a server being in point in time recovery mode and an ordinary replica
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch adds a SQL function that reports whether a standby.signal file was found at startup, so a server in point-in-time recovery can be told apart from a standby; pg_is_in_recovery() returns true in both cases. After review, the design changed to track recovery state as bitmask flags in XLogRecoveryCtlData and expose them as a text array.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Fujii Masao asked whether pg_last_wal_receive_lsn() already covers the need, since it returns NULL in archive recovery and a valid LSN in standby mode, apart from the time before the WAL receiver starts. The thread shows no reply from the author before the entry was returned with feedback four months later. Earlier, Michael Paquier objected to adding more state to XLogRecoveryCtlData, and the patch was reworked into recovery flag bitmasks.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: Wouldn't pg_last_wal_receive_lsn() be almost sufficient for the purpose?

precedents_retrieved.title: Fix PGXS so built control files work with VPATH builds
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch changes pgxs.mk so that the $(EXTENSION).control file is found along the VPATH instead of only in $(srcdir). Extensions that generate their control file could then do VPATH builds from a read-only source tree.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Peter Eisentraut offered a simpler patch using vpathsearch, which Craig Ringer rejected because it depends on the VPATH variable rather than vpath directives. No one answered Craig's follow-up. The CFBot then reported failures in the test_extensions and test_extdepend suites, and with no new version the entry was returned with feedback.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
With the thread stalled and the tests still failing, I've marked this patch
Returned with Feedback.

precedents_retrieved.title: Add more TAP coverage for archive status with crash recovery of standbys
precedents_retrieved.summary:
Add more TAP coverage for archive status with crash recovery of standbys
Reverted commit(s): Remove some unstable parts from new TAP test for archive status check
precedents_retrieved.objection:
This part of the test was included originally in 4e87c48, but got
reverted as of f9c1b8d because of timing issues in the test, where,
after more analysis, we found that the standbys may not have recovered
from the archives all the segments needed by the test.  This stabilizes
the test by making sure that standbys replay up to the position returned
by pg_switch_wal(), meaning that all segments are recovered before the
manual checkpoint that tests WAL segment recycling and its interactions
with archive status files.

roaster_notes.note: No precedent found: the precedent search returned no row about this or a related idea. Message #1 points to an earlier discussion ([0]) where Heikki raised the bug; the thread reports only that he suggested the redo-path fix and a control-file start value, and nothing there reads as a rejection.

The contract change touches only pg_get_multixact_stats(), which is new in 19 and not yet in a released branch, so no released query, dump or client changes behaviour. Heikki raised the loss of the correct num_mxids and oldest_multixact on a standby in message #4, and the thread chose an error in messages #3 and #6; the error reuses the xlogfuncs.c message and SQLSTATE that existing recovery-restricted functions already use. Not checkable without v2: whether the docs state that the function fails during recovery.

The agreed direction (v2) makes pg_get_multixact_stats() raise an error during recovery. That changes no WAL record, control file field, catalog, on-disk format or wire message, so pg_upgrade, replay, mixed-version standbys and ABI are not affected. v1's redo-side update of oldestOffset in shared memory is superseded in the thread, and the control-file option that would need a catversion bump was deferred in message #4.

The fix changes how an existing monitoring function computes or refuses to report multixact member counts on a standby. It adds no new privilege, data exposure, escalation path or unbounded resource use, and an error during recovery exposes less than before. Who may call pg_get_multixact_stats() could not be checked from the material, but the proposal does not change it.

No maintenance or fit objection holds. The agreed direction, raising an error from pg_get_multixact_stats() during recovery, adds no hot-path work, no new state, no external dependency and no new translatable strings. It reuses the xlogfuncs.c error messages. The function is new in 19, so no released monitoring depends on it. Michael, a committer, said in message #7 that he will make the change, so ownership is clear. The open items are not maintenance or fit questions: whether v1's redo-path update is also kept, the docs and the tests, and the deferred control-file field.

No existing feature gives correct member counts on a standby. pg_control_checkpoint() exposes next_multi_offset but not the oldest offset, so this is a bug fix to a new core function rather than a duplicate. The agreed error during recovery copies the existing xlogfuncs.c practice and reuses its messages, so it adds no new mechanism.

This is a bug fix for wrong output from a new function, so it needs no demand evidence beyond the reproduced mismatch in message #1. The agreed direction, an error during recovery, adds no feature surface, and committers Heikki and Michael are engaged.
